content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends amphotericin B deoxycholate as the initial treatment of choice for neonates and infants under 2 months of age at a dose of 1 mg/kg/day administered intravenously. However, caution must be exercised due to its potential nephrotoxic and ototoxic effects, especially when combined with other drugs. 1. Amikacin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 2. Cidofovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination heightens nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Iodinated Contrast Media and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Cyclosporine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs elevate the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 5. Ioversol and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Neomycin (oral) and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Streptozocin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Their concurrent use is contraindicated. 8. Tacrolimus and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination heightens nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Teicoplanin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Acyclovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 11. Atracurium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 12. Capreomycin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 13. Carboplatin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs heighten nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 14. Cephaloridine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 15. Cisatracurium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 16. Cisplatin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 17. Colistin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 18. Corticotropin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 19. Digoxin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Hypokalemia induced by amphotericin B can further increase digoxin toxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 20. Gentamicin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 21. Oxaliplatin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs heighten nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 22. Pancuronium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 23. Polymyxin B and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 24. Rapacuronium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 25. Rocuronium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 26. Saccharomyces boulardii and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 27. Succinylcholine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 28. Tobramycin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 29. Vecuronium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 30. Adefovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 31. Beclomethasone (inhaled) and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Beclomethasone increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Corticosteroids may enhance the hypokalemic effect of amphotericin B. 32. Benazepril and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Either drug increases the effects of the other through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Captopril and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs lower blood pressure. Monitor blood pressure closely when used together. 34. Deflazacort and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Dichlorphenamide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels and can cause metabolic acidosis. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 36. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Foscarnet and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 38. Ifosfamide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Ifosfamide increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for renal toxicity, bronchospasm, and hypotension. 39. Iloprost and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Either drug increases the effects of the other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider discontinuing other vasodilators to mitigate additive hypotensive effects. 40. Lomustine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Lomustine increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for renal toxicity, bronchospasm, and hypotension. 41. Mechlorethamine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Mechlorethamine increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for renal toxicity, bronchospasm, and hypotension. 42. Melphalan and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Melphalan increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for renal toxicity, bronchospasm, and hypotension. 43. Methoxyflurane and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 44. Mometasone (inhaled) and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Mometasone increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate. Corticosteroids may enhance the hypokalemic effect of amphotericin B. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Oxaliplatin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Oxaliplatin increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for renal toxicity, bronchospasm, and hypotension. 46. Paromomycin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Pentamidine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 48. Peramivir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate increases peramivir levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Rituximab and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor for signs of renal failure. 50. Rituximab-Hyaluronidase and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor for signs of renal failure. 51. Ropinterferon Alfa-2b and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Ropinterferon increases the levels or effects of amphotericin B deoxycholate. Monitor for toxicities, especially in patients receiving CYP450 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 52. Magnesium Sulfate/Potassium Chloride and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Chloride/Magnesium Sulfate/Polyethylene Glycol and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 54. Streptomycin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 55. Tenofovir DF and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination may also increase tenofovir levels. 56. Tobramycin (inhaled) and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce ototoxicity risk. 57. Triamcinolone Acetonide Injectable Suspension and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Ustekinumab and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Ustekinumab may alter CYP450 enzyme formation during chronic inflammation. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients receiving CYP450 substrates. 59. Vancomycin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 60. Voclosporin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity risks. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 61. Xipamide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration increases the risk of hypokalemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Amobarbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amobarbital decreases amphotericin B levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 63. Budesonide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 64. Butabarbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Butabarbital decreases amphotericin B levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 65. Butalbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Butalbital decreases amphotericin B levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 66. Cortisone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 67. Cosyntropin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 68. Deflazacort and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 69. Dexamethasone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 70. Flucytosine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Flucytosine increases the effects of amphotericin B deoxycholate through pharmacodynamic synergy. Amphotericin B deoxycholate increases flucytosine levels by decreasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. 71. Fludrocortisone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 72. Ganciclovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Ganciclovir increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is unknown. 73. Hydrocortisone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 74. Magnesium Chloride and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases magnesium chloride levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 75. Magnesium Citrate and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases magnesium citrate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 76. Magnesium Hydroxide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 77. Magnesium Oxide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases magnesium oxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 78. Magnesium Sulfate and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases magnesium sulfate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 79. Mestranol and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases mestranol levels by increasing metabolism. This may also cause menstrual irregularities. The clinical significance is unknown. 80. Methylprednisolone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 81. Pentobarbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Pentobarbital decreases amphotericin B levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 82. The clinical significance is unknown. 85. Potassium Citrate and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases potassium citrate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 86. Prednisolone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The interaction mechanism is unspecified, but there is a potential for hypokalemia.
